security_invariant: Percent-encoded reserved path bytes must remain escaped until they can be interpreted without becoming live path syntax.
attacker_controlled_source: Percent-encoded bytes in a URI path supplied for parsing, normalization, or equality comparison.
missing_or_incorrect_control: The vulnerable flow decodes the whole path and later re-encodes it, allowing encoded dot or slash bytes to become reserved path delimiters.
sensitive_operation: Path normalization and serialization used for URI comparison or downstream routing decisions.
vulnerable_behavior: Encoded dot segments can become active traversal syntax during parse, normalization, or equality processing.
fixed_behavior: Percent escapes are normalized while reserved delimiters stay escaped; only context-safe unreserved bytes are decoded.
root_cause: The vulnerable parser decodes percent-encoded reserved path characters and then re-encodes them, allowing encoded dot segments to become active path syntax instead of remaining escaped.
required_evidence: Trace percent-encoded path bytes through parse and serialization.
Show that reserved dot or slash escapes become path delimiters.
Distinguish the issue from ordinary URI canonicalization.
refutation_checks: Check whether encoded reserved bytes remain escaped end to end.
Check whether downstream consumers treat the result as a path.
